name: Erin Roche
life: “I still remember splitting a tip meant for the absent worker.” Saturday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Erin can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I work the deli counter. The first paid rider wants the tips I used to divide among the cooks.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for an olive canvas jacket and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Erin has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, with a center part and straight chestnut hair. Erin starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Erin has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To divide current tips with the paid rider.
family: Denise Barker is Erin’s half-sibling. Erin gets to change the plan. Denise offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The savings club*, Denise says, “I used to draw the winning number with my mother.”
connections: Tom Clement. A walking courier and the person dividing the tips need a clear agreement on the charged delivery. Also in the story is Penelope Tang (former volunteer rider).

reactions.situation: A housebound customer cannot afford the delivery fee
reactions.response: Erin asks whether combining a delivery with a willing neighbor would help.

reactions.response: Erin asks each person to say what they believe is actually owed before anybody proposes a payment.
